L01.note: -9, -36, -144 form a x4 chain and -36 is its centre, the usual position of a key surrounded by scale-error distractors.

L02.note: Two reciprocal pairs (11/4,4/11) and (11/3,3/11) cancel each other out; nothing separates 3 from 4.

L03.note: 3 is the hub: -3 is its sign flip, 6 its double, 9 its triple.

L04.note: 5 = -(-2 + -3) so it is faintly built from the others, but 14 is unexplained.

L05.note: no signal beyond -13 being the extreme of the three negatives.

L06.note: 5, 15, 45 is a x3 chain and 15 is its centre; 53/9 is the stray bad-algebra value.

L07.note: a complete -2/-4/-8/-16 power chain with no centre, so every option is equally derivable.

L08.note: -3 is the sign-flip of 3, marking 3 as the source value.

L09.note: 4, 32, 128 are powers of two with 32 in the middle (4 x 32 = 128); 36 is the near-miss decoy.

L10.note: 24/5 and 24/7 share a numerator family with 6 = 24/4, so the key sits in that family and 36 is the square-error decoy.

L11.note: -3 and -2 are adjacent, 0 and 10 unrelated; no real discriminator.

L13.note: 12 is built from the others (3 + 9) and sits between them in the multiples-of-3 set.

L14.note: -19.5 is the only non-integer, the value that looks computed rather than rounded off it.

L15.note: 27 and 3 are power-related and 2, 18 unrelated; direction of the relation is unreadable.

L16.note: -9/5 is assembled from the other options' own components (9 and 5), the usual shape of a key surrounded by its parts.

L17.note: two off-by-one twins (13,14) and (3,4); nothing picks a side.

L18.note: -8 is the sign flip of 8, making 8 the source; 2 and 16 are scale errors off it.

L19.note: 403 is the only non-round value, with 400 as the rounded decoy and 1200/120 as scale errors.

L20.note: three half-integers against one integer, but no way to rank the halves.

L22.note: thirds family with 9 as the odd integer; 11/3 is central but that is not evidence.

L23.note: 26/3 and -26/3 are a sign-flip pair, so the key is one of them; the positive is the unreversed form.

L24.note: 11 is the odd magnitude, which is only a weak tell here.

L25.note: 16, 18, 21 cluster and -4 is the sign decoy; no ranking inside the cluster.

L27.note: -209/4 is the most designed value - a quarter-denominator result of the kind completing the square produces, with -5/2 and -71 as the crude decoys.

L28.note: 14 and 21 share a factor of 7 but the direction is unreadable.

L29.note: 11/4 and 13/4 straddle 3 symmetrically; no way to choose between them.

L31.note: 5/3 is the product of two other options (5/2 x 2/3), but that is as easily a distractor construction.

L32.note: 1 and -1 are a sign pair and -16 an outlier; 11 chosen with no real basis.
